G2; Source gap; MATERIAL; Covenant ratios at 2026-05-31 and the terms of the December 2025 amendment to the credit agreement beyond its higher commitment and later maturity are not stated; covenant levels and ratios are available only at 2025-08-31; Fundamental credit; Legal & covenants; Covenant capacity; Covenant headroom at the latest date is not calculable; selected modules state the 2025-08-31 position with its date; Supply the credit agreement with its amendments and the latest compliance figures; Open

G3; Source gap; MINOR; Rating levels and outlooks are not stated in any document; Fundamental credit; Ratings & triggers; Ratings are stated as not established; Supply agency ratings with dates if the analysis needs them; Open

G4; Source gap; MINOR; Proxy statement not supplied; board composition, ownership and executive pay sit in it; Business & governance; Governance is limited to the annual report business section and one board appointment release; Supply the 2026 proxy statement; Open

G5; Source gap; MINOR; No scheduled repayment table after the November 2025 notes; the annual ladder is at 2025-08-31. Maturities can be read from the instrument names in the latest debt note; Financial foundation; Refinancing & LME; Maturity wall is built from instrument names and flagged as such; None required for the snapshot; Open

G6; Definition conflict; MINOR; Issuer net leverage adjusted for acquisitions, core EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA differ from covenant EBITDA and from net debt over reported EBITDA; the issuer figure adds expected precast EBITDA and removes acquisition costs; Financial foundation; Fundamental credit; Leverage must be computed from reported debt and stated EBITDA with the definition named; the issuer figure is context only; Name the definition beside every leverage figure; Open

G7; Perimeter and period break; MINOR; Foley and CP&P were acquired in December 2025 and USD 2,000,000 thousand of notes issued in November 2025, so year-end 2025-08-31 comparisons are not like-for-like; Financial foundation; Fundamental credit; Comparisons across the break carry a stated limitation; Show post-balance-sheet effects beside any year-end figure; Open

facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 0.34x at the 2024 year end to 0.71x at the 2025 year end and 2.47x at 2026-05-31, and the rise comes from debt rather than weaker earnings. The 2025 year-end net debt of USD 311,043 thousand is not like-for-like: pro forma net debt is USD 986,043 thousand (2.25x) after the Concrete Pipe and Precast acquisition on 2025-12-01 and USD 2,151,043 thousand (4.90x) after the Foley acquisition on 2025-12-15, each on year-end EBITDA that holds none of the acquired earnings. Creditors therefore hold a far larger claim at 2026-05-31, with net debt of USD 2,840,726 thousand, supported by earnings that have absorbed the precast businesses for less than six months. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 92

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Medium: Covenant ratios at 2026-05-31 and the terms of the amended credit agreement beyond its higher commitment and later maturity are not stated; levels of 2.50x minimum interest cover and 0.60x maximum debt to capitalization and reported ratios are available only at 2025-08-31, so covenant headroom at the latest date cannot be calculated. Closing this needs the compliance figures and the credit agreement. - Medium: Indentures and guarantor lists are not in the sources, so guarantor scope for the notes is not stated and the security and ranking of the tax-exempt bonds, finance leases, Poland receivables advances and other borrowings, USD 528,920 thousand in total, are not stated; they are left out of the debt stack and its cumulative leverage. - Medium: No statements after 2026-05-31 are in the sources, so the year ended 2026-08-31 and its leverage are not available; the latest balance sheet is 171 days before the as-of date. Closing this needs the fiscal 2026 annual report or results release if published. - Medium: The issuer's net leverage adjusted for acquisitions of 2.1x cannot be reproduced because the precast results since acquisition are not stated, and the USD 245 million of expected annualized EBITDA it substitutes is a management estimate. Leverage here uses reported figures only. - Low: The quarterly report gives no maturity year for short-term borrowings of USD 33,012 thousand and other borrowings of USD 8,819 thousand, and no repayment schedule after the November 2025 notes; finance leases of USD 192,029 thousand are outside the ladder, and the Series 2025 Bonds have a mandatory tender on 2032-05-15 although they mature in 2055. The ladder is therefore partial and flagged as such. - Low: The first and second quarters of fiscal 2026 are not tabulated in the statement tables; their adjusted EBITDA appears in the issuer's quarterly reconciliation, and the last twelve months are built from the annual and nine-month columns. - Low: Lines the source prints as a dash are shown as not supplied rather than zero: litigation expense and accrued contingent litigation-related loss in FY2024, acquisitions in FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2025, government assistance in FY2024 and the first nine months of 2026, and the proceeds from issuance of long-term debt in FY2024; debt issuance costs and committed financing fees are likewise blank where the source prints no line. - Low: Asset impairments are not a separate line in the quarterly statements, so interim columns show them as not supplied; the first nine months of 2025 amount of USD 1,171 thousand appears only in the issuer's reconciliation. - Low: Restricted cash is not a separate line in the annual report balance sheet for FY2024 and FY2025 and assets held for sale are not a separate line in the latest quarterly balance sheet; the quarterly comparative shows USD 2,652 thousand of restricted cash at 2025-08-31 with totals unchanged. - Low: Other noncurrent liabilities of USD 273,445 thousand include operating lease liabilities of USD 180,846 thousand and other items that the balance sheet does not split, so pension and other non-debt obligations are not separately stated there; the pension funded status is a small liability. - Low: Capital expenditures are shown in total because the sources give no maintenance and growth split, and no single-period segment margin for the last twelve months is constructed. - Low: The 2033 and 2035 notes were issued in November 2025 with no day stated, and the aggregate dividend declared on 2026-06-24 is not stated, so neither has a pro forma net debt figure.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a more levered, integration-dependent view is operating momentum and the issuer's own path: core EBITDA margin of 14.2% in the latest quarter, precast adjusted EBITDA of USD 86.5 million in nine months against a management expectation of USD 245 million annualized, and a stated aim of leverage below 2x ahead of mid-2027. That view would win if fiscal 2026 results show a full year of precast earnings near the expectation, free cash flow applied to debt rather than buybacks, and the tariff intact. It would lose if the Pacific Steel Group accrual of USD 373,476 thousand is paid in cash, if the tariff is relaxed and margins narrow, or if integration costs and capital spending for the West Virginia mill stay high. facts.label: Competitive and external forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high and the main force on margin: the 2025 annual report describes global steelmaking capacity far above demand and import competition, so price takers lose margin first when imports return; buyer power is moderate because fabricated rebar is generally sold through competitive bids, often on fixed-price projects; supplier power is moderate because scrap and energy prices swing, partly offset by company-owned recycling; new entrants are limited by the capital needed for a mill and substitutes for rebar are few. The tariff and the European carbon border mechanism are the policy factors that matter to credit: the tariff supports U.S. margin and its removal is the largest external risk, while the European mechanism improved Polish volumes and carbon cost assistance of USD 36.0 million was received in nine months against USD 48.1 million a year earlier, so Europe Steel Group earnings partly depend on government payments. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position are strong: net sales of USD 7,798,480 thousand and a self-described leading position in U.S. rebar give shock absorption. Competitive advantage is average: integration and cost position help, but products are commodity-priced and margin relies on tariffs. Business diversification is average: North America Steel Group is 75.1% of net sales in nine months and the United States 79.7% of fiscal 2025 sales, with precast and Europe adding limited offset. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital spending is 5.80% of last-twelve-months net sales and part of it ends when the West Virginia mill is finished, but power-intensive mills carry high fixed cost. Margin stability is weak: adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.22%, 5.65% and 13.04% across fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and the last twelve months. Free cash flow stability is average: it was USD 575,437 thousand, USD 312,249 thousand and USD 405,038 thousand in the same periods, positive but variable. Ability to refinance is average: USD 2,000 million of notes were placed in November 2025 and the first large maturity is in January 2030, but ratings are not stated. Liquidity is average: committed liquidity of USD 1,558,789 thousand covers identified near-term claims 1.10x before operating cash flow. Financial policy and governance are average: independent board and a stated leverage goal, offset by continued buybacks and a higher dividend while leverage rose; these are analyst assessments, not ratings. Basis: calculation M4; calculation M5; calculation M6; calculation M8; calculation M9; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside begins with a relaxation of import protection or a construction slowdown that narrows steel prices against scrap, and mills first lose margin per ton; as legacy earnings fall back to the fiscal 2025 level before the litigation charge, EBITDA drops while interest of USD 170.9 million a year, capital spending and the litigation accrual do not. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, CMC presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, integration and domestic leadership, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rose to 2.47x after debt-funded acquisitions, run-rate interest cover of 6.72x and a litigation accrual outside debt. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The 12 supplied documents are sufficient for a credit snapshot of COMMERCIAL METALS Co, but only with limits: covenant headroom, ratings and the year ended 2026-08-31 cannot be assessed from them. The set holds two annual reports, three 2026 quarterly reports and seven press releases; the latest balance sheet is dated 2026-05-31, 171 days before the as-of date.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 3

The credit agreement and note terms, rating levels, the proxy statement and any report for the year ended 2026-08-31 are not in the set. Conclusions on leverage and liquidity therefore rest on filings dated up to 2026-06-29, and covenant levels come from the 2025 annual report. The issuer's own leverage figure uses acquisition adjustments and is not comparable with leverage computed from reported debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4

## Request

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage reached 2.47x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-05-31 after debt-funded acquisitions, a much heavier claim on cash flow than before, though liquidity stays ample. Total debt is 2.96x EBITDA, and the acquisitions, USD 2,516,122 thousand net of cash acquired, contribute earnings only since December 2025, so a full-year view would show less leverage; the issuer's own adjusted figure is 2.1x.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4

Interest cover of 13.46x on cash interest paid flatters the position because the new notes paid only part of a year of coupons; against interest payable over the next twelve months, cover is 6.72x. A litigation accrual of USD 373,476 thousand sits outside debt and would lift net leverage to 2.80x if treated as debt-like.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 50
### Analysis by dimension

Net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 0.34x at the 2024 year end to 0.71x at the 2025 year end and 2.47x at 2026-05-31, and the rise comes from debt rather than weaker earnings. The 2025 year-end net debt of USD 311,043 thousand is not like-for-like: pro forma net debt is USD 986,043 thousand (2.25x) after the Concrete Pipe and Precast acquisition on 2025-12-01 and USD 2,151,043 thousand (4.90x) after the Foley acquisition on 2025-12-15, each on year-end EBITDA that holds none of the acquired earnings. Creditors therefore hold a far larger claim at 2026-05-31, with net debt of USD 2,840,726 thousand, supported by earnings that have absorbed the precast businesses for less than six months.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 92

Coverage is strong on its face but overstated. Cash interest paid over the last twelve months was USD 85,268 thousand, giving cover of 13.46x, yet the 2033 and 2035 senior unsecured notes, USD 2,000,000 thousand in total, were issued in November 2025 and paid only part of a year of coupons. Interest payable over the next twelve months is USD 170.9 million, which puts run-rate cover at 6.72x on reported EBITDA that itself includes the acquisitions only from December 2025.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 50

Cash-flow quality is adequate but not yet strong. Operating cash flow of USD 918,228 thousand over the last twelve months less capital expenditures of USD 513,190 thousand leaves free cash flow of USD 405,038 thousand, or 0.35x EBITDA, and nine months of working capital absorbed USD 195,098 thousand, which the issuer attributes to higher materials costs in inventories and higher selling prices in receivables. Capital spending of about USD 550 million is planned for fiscal 2026, driven by the fourth micro mill in West Virginia, so free cash flow stays well below operating cash flow while that build continues.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49

Liquidity covers the visible near-term claims. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand and the undrawn revolver, available after USD 1.0 million of letters of credit, give committed liquidity of USD 1,558,789 thousand, and USD 1,768,475 thousand on the issuer's wider basis, against current maturities of USD 88,792 thousand, a litigation accrual of USD 373,476 thousand whose payment timing is uncertain, and purchase obligations of about USD 780 million due within twelve months. The revolver of USD 1,000 million matures on 2030-12-17.
Basis: calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52

Strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own message that leverage is falling toward less than 2x ahead of its mid-2027 goal, supported by core EBITDA margin of 14.2% in the latest quarter and expected annualized precast EBITDA of USD 245 million that its 2.1x measure includes. That view would win if the fiscal 2026 results show a full year of precast earnings, free cash flow near the current run-rate and cash used to repay debt; it would lose if the litigation accrual is paid in cash or capital spending stays high, because net debt would then rise rather than fall.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1 and 4; calculation C12

Data and definition risks are contained but real. Reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer prints none, the issuer changed its adjusted EBITDA definition in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 and recast prior periods, and fiscal 2025 EBITDA carries the litigation charge of USD 362,272 thousand, which inflates fiscal 2025 total debt to EBITDA to 3.09x. The issuer's 2.1x measure cannot be reproduced because actual precast results since acquisition are not stated, so leverage here is computed from reported figures only.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 60

## Findings
### Bottom line

CMC remains a cyclical, vertically integrated steel and construction-products group, but its credit profile now rests on integrating two debt-funded precast acquisitions that changed the company more than any operating shift did. Precast delivered adjusted EBITDA of USD 86.5 million in nine months, and the issuer's 2.1x net leverage reproduces at 2.12x from its own inputs, which corrects the Financial foundation statement that it could not be reproduced.
Basis: calculation K2; calculation K3; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 45; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4

The shareholder base is listed and widely held with no controlling holder identified, and nine of ten directors are independent; the proxy statement that would confirm control rights is not supplied. Dividends rose 11% in March 2026 and buybacks of USD 76.1 million continued alongside USD 2,000 million of new notes, so creditor alignment rests on the stated aim of leverage below 2x by mid-2027.

Basis: 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX99.1_2026-02-28_cmc_d117730dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Key findings

- The precast acquisitions are the dominant credit event, and they were mostly debt-funded: Foley, the larger purchase, was paid from the 2033 and 2035 senior unsecured notes, whose net proceeds equal 78.9% of the USD 2,516,122 thousand of cash paid net of cash acquired for both purchases, and Concrete Pipe and Precast was paid from cash on hand. Goodwill and intangibles make up 81.9% of the allocated price, so little tangible asset value stands behind the new debt, and the businesses added net sales of USD 320.3 million and pre-tax earnings of USD 24,625 thousand since closing.
Basis: calculation K2; calculation K4; calculation K5; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–15

- The legacy base is cyclical but integrated and, for now, supported by trade policy. North America Steel Group supplies 75.1% of net sales and 77.7% of segment adjusted EBITDA in nine months, its metal margin per ton rose 27%, and a 50% tariff on most steel imports props up domestic prices; relaxation of that tariff is the main external risk to the margin.
Basis: calculation K1; calculation K6; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 44

- The issuer's leverage measure is reproducible, which corrects the earlier Financial foundation statement. Net debt of USD 2,865,703 thousand on the issuer's definition over adjusted EBITDA adjusted for expected annualized precast EBITDA of USD 245 million gives 2.12x, so the 2.1x depends on that management expectation rather than on reported precast results.
Basis: calculation K3; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Ownership and governance look conventional for a listed company but control rights are not established. The board has ten directors with nine independent and a separate chairman, and the auditor has served for decades, yet the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indentures are not supplied, so holders above five percent, restricted payment capacity and guarantor scope are not known; the sponsor and governance risk level is medium on that evidence.
Basis: 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 139; EX99.1_2026-02-28_cmc_d117730dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Shareholder returns continued while debt rose. Buybacks and dividends took USD 138,234 thousand in nine months, 22.9% of operating cash flow, and the dividend was raised 11% in March 2026; this is moderate in size but is discretionary cash that could repay debt after a debt-funded acquisition.
Basis: calculation K8; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Litigation is the main event risk outside debt. A jury verdict of USD 110.0 million for Pacific Steel Group, trebled by the court, is accrued at USD 373,476 thousand in current liabilities with payment timing uncertain, and a second suit seeking about USD 29 million has no accrual; the company is appealing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

- Disclosure is frequent and reconciled, with one correction. The latest quarterly report corrected pro forma net sales that the second-quarter report overstated by USD 75.1 million, which the company judged not material; reported statements were not affected.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a more levered, integration-dependent view is operating momentum and the issuer's own path: core EBITDA margin of 14.2% in the latest quarter, precast adjusted EBITDA of USD 86.5 million in nine months against a management expectation of USD 245 million annualized, and a stated aim of leverage below 2x ahead of mid-2027. That view would win if fiscal 2026 results show a full year of precast earnings near the expectation, free cash flow applied to debt rather than buybacks, and the tariff intact. It would lose if the Pacific Steel Group accrual of USD 373,476 thousand is paid in cash, if the tariff is relaxed and margins narrow, or if integration costs and capital spending for the West Virginia mill stay high.

Basis: calculation K3; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 45; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that control is dispersed rests on holders of record and board independence only; a concentrated holder above five percent, or related-party dealings, would change the governance view.

- The credit agreement, indentures and guarantor lists are not supplied, so the conclusion on creditor alignment cannot be tied to restricted payment or debt capacity; a basket that permits larger distributions would worsen it.

- No document after 2026-06-29 is supplied, so whether the fourth quarter and the stated deleveraging aim were delivered is not established; the leverage path conclusion is provisional until fiscal 2026 results are read.

- Precast adjusted EBITDA is stated only as a contribution to the change in segment results and as management's expectation, so the reproduced 2.12x leverage is issuer-defined and would move with a different annualized figure.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

CMC completed two cash acquisitions in December 2025 that created a precast platform: Concrete Pipe and Precast, LLC on 2025-12-01 for about USD 675 million from cash on hand, and the holding companies that own Foley Products Company, LLC on 2025-12-15 for about USD 1.84 billion. Foley was funded from the proceeds of the 2033 and 2035 senior unsecured notes, USD 1,000 million each, issued in November 2025, which raised net proceeds of USD 1,985,000 thousand. ## Findings
### Bottom line

CMC is an adequate but cyclical credit whose leverage rose sharply because debt paid for two precast acquisitions, so creditors now depend on acquired and legacy earnings holding up through the integration. Net leverage was 2.47x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-05-31, the pro forma figure for the dividend declared on 2026-06-24 is not established, run-rate interest cover is 6.72x, and committed liquidity is USD 1,558,789 thousand.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The main downside is a fall in tariff-supported steel margins while interest, capital spending and a USD 373,476 thousand litigation accrual stay fixed; on earnings at the fiscal 2025 level before the litigation charge, net leverage would be 3.54x, or 2.71x if precast reaches its expected USD 245 million a year.
Basis: calculation M7; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Key findings

- Leverage is the dominant constraint and it is new. Net leverage at 2026-05-31 was 2.47x and total debt 2.96x of reported EBITDA, after USD 2,000 million of senior unsecured notes and cash funded USD 2,516,122 thousand of acquisitions; at the 2025 year end net leverage was 0.71x, or 2.25x pro forma for the acquisition on 2025-12-01 and 4.90x pro forma for the acquisition on 2025-12-15.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Business quality is the strongest support. The company is the largest U.S. rebar manufacturer and fabricator on its own description, runs scrap recycling, mills and fabrication as one chain, and North America Steel Group earned 77.7% of segment adjusted EBITDA; the integrated chain and a fabrication backlog give more visibility than a pure mill, though products are commodity-priced.
Basis: calculation M9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Cash generation is solid but heavily absorbed. Free cash flow of USD 405,038 thousand over the last twelve months is 0.35x of EBITDA after capital spending of USD 513,190 thousand, and about USD 550 million is planned for fiscal 2026 for the West Virginia mill, so deleveraging comes mainly from earnings growth rather than free cash flow.
Basis: calculation M4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 48

- Liquidity is adequate near term but not a large surplus. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand and the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver give USD 1,558,789 thousand committed, which is 1.10x the identified near-term claims of USD 1,413,168 thousand before any operating cash flow, with the revolver running to 2030-12-17.
Basis: calculation M5; calculation M6; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

- Interest cover reads better than the run-rate. Cover on cash interest paid is 13.46x, but the new notes carry an annual coupon of USD 117,500 thousand and interest payable over the next twelve months is USD 170.9 million, so run-rate cover is 6.72x.
Basis: calculation M3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Financial policy is average: the board is independent and a leverage goal below 2x by mid-2027 is stated, but buybacks and a higher dividend continued while debt rose, and restricted payment capacity is not established. The litigation accrual of USD 373,476 thousand is 13.15% of net debt and sits outside debt.
Basis: calculation M12; calculation M13; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious view is earnings momentum and the issuer's path: adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.04% over the last twelve months against 5.65% in fiscal 2025, precast adjusted EBITDA of USD 86.5 million in nine months, and a stated aim of leverage below 2x. Business & governance reproduced the issuer's 2.1x as 2.12x from its own inputs, which supersedes the Financial foundation statement that it could not be reproduced. That view would win if fiscal 2026 results show reported net leverage moving toward that 2.12x, free cash flow applied to debt and no cash payment of the litigation accrual. The cautious view would hold or strengthen if steel margins narrow after any relaxation of tariffs, if capital spending stays high, or if the accrual is paid from cash.
Basis: calculation M8; calculation M10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37
### Limitations

- Covenant ratios at 2026-05-31 and the terms of the amended credit agreement are not stated, so the liquidity and leverage-tolerance assessments are not tested against covenant headroom; a ratio close to its limit would make liquidity less comfortable than shown.

- No agency ratings or market prices are supplied, so the refinancing capacity judgement rests on the successful issue of USD 2,000 million of notes in November 2025 and the enlarged revolver; weaker market access later would lower it.

- The latest statements end on 2026-05-31, so delivery of the fourth quarter outlook and any year-end leverage are not established; the downside scenario is built from fiscal 2025 results and the issuer's expectation for precast, and moves with both.

- Restricted payment and debt capacity are not established because the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the view that capital returns are modest relative to cash flow cannot be set against what the documents permit.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: scale and integration. CMC reports net sales of USD 7,798,480 thousand and says it is the largest U.S. rebar manufacturer and fabricator, with recycling, mills and fabrication in one chain that secures scrap and keeps its mills loaded; this lowers input and demand risk compared with a stand-alone mill and supports cash generation through the cycle.
Basis: calculation M9; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 13

Strength: trade protection and demand visibility. A 50% tariff on most steel imports supports domestic prices, and fabrication backlog of USD 845.7 million of remaining obligations with about 70% due within twelve months gives visibility for North America fabrication; this supports margin and cash flow while the tariff stands.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37

Strength: liquidity and market access. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand, an undrawn revolver of USD 1,000 million to 2030-12-17 and a USD 2,000 million note issue in November 2025 show lenders and the bond market funded a large acquisition programme; this lowers near-term refinancing risk.
Basis: calculation M5; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 22

Strength: earnings recovery and precast contribution. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 1,154,161 thousand over the last twelve months, a 13.04% margin, and precast added USD 86.5 million in nine months; this lifts debt service capacity if it persists.
Basis: calculation M8; calculation M10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions. Net leverage of 2.47x at 2026-05-31, against 0.71x at the 2025 year end, shrinks the cushion against a margin squeeze, and goodwill and intangibles are 81.9% of the allocated acquisition price, so little tangible value backs the new debt.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: interest and capital spending absorb cash. Run-rate interest of USD 170.9 million and capital spending of about USD 550 million this year leave free cash flow at 0.35x of EBITDA and make deleveraging depend on earnings.
Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 50

Weakness: cyclical, commodity-priced earnings with policy exposure. Fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 5.65% (10.30% before the litigation charge) against 12.22% a year earlier, showing how quickly margin can compress when steel prices fall relative to scrap, and the tariff that supports prices could be relaxed.
Basis: calculation M8; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 12

Weakness: litigation outside debt. The Pacific Steel Group judgment is accrued at USD 373,476 thousand with payment timing uncertain, and a second suit seeking about USD 29 million has no accrual; a cash payment would draw on liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

Opportunity: the fourth micro mill in West Virginia is due to start production in 2026 and the precast platform can grow with infrastructure demand, both of which would raise earnings if delivered; threat: tariff relaxation, import resurgence, integration problems and a rise in scrap or energy costs would each lower margin and cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 12

### Business and ownership

CMC is a vertically integrated North American and Polish steel and construction-products group that recycles scrap, melts it in electric arc furnaces, rolls rebar, merchant bar and wire rod, and fabricates reinforcing steel; since December 2025 it also makes precast concrete and pipe products. Net sales were USD 7,798,480 thousand in fiscal 2025, 79.7% of them in the United States, and North America Steel Group supplied 78.0% of external net sales and 77.7% of segment adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, so the credit rests mainly on U.S. rebar economics. The business is cyclical, seasonal and commodity-priced, with net sales higher in the third and fourth quarters, which makes interim leverage swing with the season.
Basis: calculation M9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 11

The company is listed with no controlling holder identified, nine of ten directors independent and a separate chairman, so there is no sponsor to extract or support and creditor alignment rests on the board and stated policy. Dividends and buybacks continued after the acquisitions, the financial policy is average, and the proxy statement, credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so ownership above five percent, restricted payment capacity and guarantor scope are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M12
### Revenue, margin and cash conversion

Revenue is driven by steel price and tons shipped. In nine months to 2026-05-31 North America steel products metal margin per ton rose 27% and tons shipped fell 3%, so earnings came from price spread rather than volume, which is more reversible; precast adds infrastructure-oriented products whose cyclicality is not yet shown in the sources, and fabrication backlog gives visibility only in North America. Customer concentration is not disclosed, so durability beyond that backlog is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 18

Margins depend on the spread between selling prices and scrap, plus power and gas, which are partly hedged; the adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.22% in fiscal 2024, 5.65% in fiscal 2025 (10.30% before the litigation charge) and 13.04% over the last twelve months, so margin has moved by several percentage points within two years. Operating leverage is high because mills run at high fixed cost, so a volume or spread decline passes quickly to EBITDA and then to free cash flow.
Basis: calculation M8; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 23

Cash conversion is moderate: capital spending is 5.80% of last-twelve-months net sales, free cash flow is 0.35x of EBITDA, and nine months of working capital absorbed USD 195,098 thousand as inventory costs and selling prices rose; capital spending is partly discretionary once the West Virginia mill is finished, which gives some flexibility over the maturity wall that begins with USD 300,000 thousand of notes due in January 2030.
Basis: calculation M4; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Competitive and external forces

Competitive rivalry is high and the main force on margin: the 2025 annual report describes global steelmaking capacity far above demand and import competition, so price takers lose margin first when imports return; buyer power is moderate because fabricated rebar is generally sold through competitive bids, often on fixed-price projects; supplier power is moderate because scrap and energy prices swing, partly offset by company-owned recycling; new entrants are limited by the capital needed for a mill and substitutes for rebar are few. The tariff and the European carbon border mechanism are the policy factors that matter to credit: the tariff supports U.S. margin and its removal is the largest external risk, while the European mechanism improved Polish volumes and carbon cost assistance of USD 36.0 million was received in nine months against USD 48.1 million a year earlier, so Europe Steel Group earnings partly depend on government payments.
Basis: 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 46
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are strong: net sales of USD 7,798,480 thousand and a self-described leading position in U.S. rebar give shock absorption. Competitive advantage is average: integration and cost position help, but products are commodity-priced and margin relies on tariffs. Business diversification is average: North America Steel Group is 75.1% of net sales in nine months and the United States 79.7% of fiscal 2025 sales, with precast and Europe adding limited offset. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital spending is 5.80% of last-twelve-months net sales and part of it ends when the West Virginia mill is finished, but power-intensive mills carry high fixed cost. Margin stability is weak: adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.22%, 5.65% and 13.04% across fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and the last twelve months. Free cash flow stability is average: it was USD 575,437 thousand, USD 312,249 thousand and USD 405,038 thousand in the same periods, positive but variable. Ability to refinance is average: USD 2,000 million of notes were placed in November 2025 and the first large maturity is in January 2030, but ratings are not stated. Liquidity is average: committed liquidity of USD 1,558,789 thousand covers identified near-term claims 1.10x before operating cash flow. Financial policy and governance are average: independent board and a stated leverage goal, offset by continued buybacks and a higher dividend while leverage rose; these are analyst assessments, not ratings.
Basis: calculation M4; calculation M5; calculation M6; calculation M8; calculation M9; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook

Over twelve to twenty-four months the issuer expects the fourth quarter core EBITDA to rise sequentially, a mill outage headwind of about USD 20 million to fall away and precast to add; leverage should fall if precast earns its expected USD 245 million a year, but this is management's view and is not confirmed by any later document. Over three to five years the West Virginia mill and precast platform lift capacity and diversification, while the company plans leverage below 2x by mid-2027, so the medium-term credit trend is improving if delivery follows, with the tariff and construction cycle as the swing factors.
Basis: calculation M10; EX99.1_2026-05-31_cmc_cmc-5312026xearningsreleas-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37
### Downside scenario

The downside begins with a relaxation of import protection or a construction slowdown that narrows steel prices against scrap, and mills first lose margin per ton; as legacy earnings fall back to the fiscal 2025 level before the litigation charge, EBITDA drops while interest of USD 170.9 million a year, capital spending and the litigation accrual do not. On net debt at 2026-05-31, net leverage would be 3.54x on that earnings level and 2.71x if precast reaches USD 245 million, so free cash flow falls toward zero, buybacks would have to stop and the company would draw first on cash of USD 559,759 thousand and then on the undrawn revolver. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because committed liquidity is 1.10x the identified near-term claims before operating cash flow, but covenant headroom is not established, and the observable triggers are metal margin per ton, tariff changes, free cash flow and the pace of buybacks.
Basis: calculation M6; calculation M7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Overall credit view

Overall, CMC presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, integration and domestic leadership, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rose to 2.47x after debt-funded acquisitions, run-rate interest cover of 6.72x and a litigation accrual outside debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive but absorbed by capital spending, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of precast earnings and on the tariff, with the first large maturity of USD 300,000 thousand in January 2030. The primary downside path is a margin squeeze in U.S. steel while interest, capital spending and litigation stay fixed. Further analysis would require covenant headroom at 2026-05-31, the credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and fiscal 2026 results. Top risk: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions combined with margin cyclicality.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
